provenance.authorship: Original project scenario, AI-assisted draft. Practitioner review and scoring calibration pending.

title: First-Time Manager: Reset an Overcommitted Week
prompt: Your five-person team has 120 available hours this week after leave and routine work. Requests total 170 hours: a contractual delivery (70), an internal dashboard (40), a customer issue investigation (30) and training (30). The investigation has no confirmed deadline or severity yet. Your director (the AI) asks you to accept everything. Negotiate a plan and explain how you will involve the team.

anchors.0: Commits to 170 hours with 120 available or treats unapproved overtime as free capacity.
anchors.2: Identifies the 50-hour gap and proposes deferral.
anchors.4: Presents a feasible allocation with explicit estimates and uncertainty; for example 70 delivery + 10 onboarding + 4 triage leaves 36 hours for chosen work and contingency, subject to actual skills.

rubric.label: Resolve uncertain priority
rubric.description: Checks impact before making a rigid commitment.

anchors.0: Drops the issue or all onboarding solely because neither is loudest.
anchors.2: Asks about the issue and required training.
anchors.4: Uses a bounded fact-finding step and conditional replan, separates required from optional work and explains who decides if the issue proves urgent.

rubric.label: Negotiate an accountable plan
rubric.description: Makes tradeoffs and team constraints visible.

anchors.0: Accepts incompatible demands or blames the team.
anchors.2: States what must move and informs stakeholders.
anchors.4: Checks skills and workload with the team, offers the director clear options, names owners and tells affected requesters what changed and when it will be reviewed.

reference.scenario: Your five-person team has 120 available hours this week after leave and routine work. Requests total 170 hours: a contractual delivery (70), an internal dashboard (40), a customer issue investigation (30) and training (30). The investigation has no confirmed deadline or severity yet. Your director (the AI) asks you to accept everything. Negotiate a plan and explain how you will involve the team.

facts.value: The dashboard can move one week without affecting an external commitment. Training has a 10-hour required onboarding component; the other 20 hours can be rescheduled.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about deadlines, obligations or movable scope

facts.value: The issue affects a small number of customers; its impact has not yet been verified. A four-hour investigation can establish whether it needs urgent escalation.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about issue severity or bounded investigation

model_points: Presents a feasible allocation with explicit estimates and uncertainty; for example 70 delivery + 10 onboarding + 4 triage leaves 36 hours for chosen work and contingency, subject to actual skills.
Uses a bounded fact-finding step and conditional replan, separates required from optional work and explains who decides if the issue proves urgent.
Checks skills and workload with the team, offers the director clear options, names owners and tells affected requesters what changed and when it will be reviewed.

probes.trigger: candidate presents an allocation above 120 hours
probes.question: Can you reconcile that plan with this week’s available capacity?
What missing information could change its priority?
Which stakeholder commitments now need updating?

fair_alternatives: A different feasible allocation can score fully if obligations and the uncertainty about customer impact are handled.
A shorter delivery scope can be negotiated if the contractual owner approves; do not assume approval.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess only the decisions and reasoning demonstrated in this fictional exercise. No hiring-readiness, personality, legal compliance or workplace performance claim follows from this score. A valid alternative can earn full credit. Unrevealed conditional facts must not be assumed known or required for credit; credit asking for needed information and a conditional plan.

interviewer_notes: You are the counterpart named in the prompt. If this is a written review, remain the hiring interviewer while the candidate reads and writes. Let the candidate finish, including thinking and self-correction. Answer only supplied facts when their reveal condition is met; otherwise say the information is unknown. Use neutral probes after a completed answer, one at a time. Do not prescribe the rubric as a spoken checklist. Accept relevant examples from work, education and community leadership. Do not request private employee records, infer protected traits, invent employment rules or promise a real organizational outcome. Simulation gives no answer before assessment; coaching may offer labeled assistance.

learning_drills.title: Make the tradeoff visible
learning_drills.prompt: Write two feasible weekly allocations and state the evidence that would make you choose between them. This is self-guided practice with no automated assessment.
